summary.text: Ken Fredette is a Republican member of the Maine House of Representatives who has represented District 33 since December 3, 2024 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
An attorney, he previously served in the Maine House from 2010 to 2018.

paragraphs.text: Ken Fredette earned a B.S. in accounting from the University of Maine at Machias, an M.S. in Public Policy and Management from the University of Southern Maine's Muskie School of Public Service, an M.S. in Administration from Harvard University's John F. Kennedy School of Government, and a J.D. from the University of Maine School of Law.
His professional experience includes serving as a Judge Advocate General, and as of his 2024 campaign he was a Colonel in the Maine Air National Guard.
Fredette served in the Maine House of Representatives for District 100 from 2010 to 2018, and during the 2015 session, as Minority Leader, he did not serve on a committee.

Earlier in that period he served on the Appropriations and Financial Affairs and Elections committees (2011-2012), the Rules and Business of the House Committee (2013-2014), and the Ethics and Rules and Business of the House committees (2017).
He returned to the House in December 2024 as the representative for District 33, and he advanced from the Republican primary on June 9, 2026.
